transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 mins
Attendees: Sofia Alvarez (Redwood AE); Marcus Chen (Redwood SE); Elliot Park (Redwood CSM); Priya Patel (AegisMed VP Eng); Tom Morales (AegisMed ML Eng); Lisa Chen (AegisMed SRE); Darren Ng (AegisMed Product)

Summary:
- Quick review of pilot telemetry and a proposal for version-fencing (ie pinning certain routes to vetted model variants) and soft-gates (automatic fallback thresholds)
- Discussed tradeoffs: latency vs cost, pinned variants vs on-demand fallback, and audit/trace requirements for rollbacks
- Agreed actions: Redwood to send trimmed results + run extra benchmark; customer to confirm freeze list and deadline

Topics covered:
- Pilot results snapshot, P95 latency, token cost estimate
- Model catalog comparison (quantized variants vs full precision)
- Rollback/escape hatch playbook: canary -> auto-fallback -> manual rollback
- Security/compliance notes for VPC/private deployment routes

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check in. um we wanted to focus today on the model fencing plan and the soft gates that you asked about.
[00:18] Priya: yep thanks Sofia. we reviewed the dashboard this morning, and the latency on the triage route spikes sometimes which is our main concern.
[00:30] Marcus: yep, so just to set expectations, the pilot has three variants in the catalog that we've been testing — the rw-neoxt-13b-quant (we called it q2), the rw-13b-fp16 baseline, and a smaller rw-4b-compact for fallback. some of the auto transcriptions earlier showed, uh, r w neo x — but that's the label.
[00:48] Tom: one quick question — are the P95 numbers you're showing with KV cache warmed or cold? that makes a big diff.
[00:56] Marcus: good call — the dashboard is mixed. most of the numbers were with a mixed traffic profile; we've got a separate warmed run which improves P95 by about 120 ms on average. i'll attach the warmed logs.
[01:12] Lisa: ok that explains the variance. our SRE cares about tail more than median.
[01:20] Sofia: so what we're proposing is: pick a freeze date for the routes you want fenced — after that we pin to a vetted variant (e.g., rw-neoxt-13b-quant-v2) and enable a soft gate: if p95 or error rate crosses threshold for N minutes, traffic automatically routes to the fallback variant, plus we trigger an alert and a canary rollback window.
[01:45] Priya: sounds reasonable. whats the rollback runway? like how fast can you switch back if the fallback is worse?
[01:53] Marcus: typically we can ghost-route in seconds and full cutover in under a minute for the same region; the bigger delay is rewarming caches if you're switching to a larger model. if you go to a smaller quantized model as fallback, it tends to be faster to boot but might change answer quality — so you need evaluation metrics to accept that.
[02:15] Darren: right and product wants to avoid user-visible regressions. can we do a shadow-route to capture outputs before full switch?
[02:22] Elliot: yes we recommend shadowing for at least one full traffic cycle (24 hrs ideally) for the high-risk routes. that lets you compare quality metrics without impacting live responses.
[02:33] Tom: about the model catalog, we noticed the labels in your deck differ from our internal names, is there a crosswalk doc?
[02:40] Sofia: yes — i'll send the mapping table. sorry about the inconsistent naming in the spreadsheet earlier.
[02:48] Priya: security question — for the fenced routes are logs going to Redwood console or do they stay inside our VPC? we need audit retention for 2 years.
[02:58] Marcus: for Private deployments logs can live in your KMS-backed storage; for Dedicated we retain trace metadata in the console but you can export full transcripts to your S3 with KMS encryption. i'll attach the security export guide.
[03:15] Lisa: and SSO and role-based access? we need to ensure only product and a narrow list of folks can trigger rollbacks.
[03:22] Sofia: RBAC + SAML SSO available; we can set a policy that only a specific group can escalate the rollback approval. that also can be gated with two-person approval for manual rollbacks.
[03:33] Priya: nice. any privacy concerns with the shadowing?
[03:36] Marcus: shadowing keeps traffic in flight to Redwood runtime but you can opt to redact or mask PII before it's persisted; we also support tokenization hooks if you want to strip sensitive fields.
[03:46] Darren: back to the soft gates, how do you compute thresholds? are they absolute ms numbers or relative to baseline?
[03:51] Marcus: typically start with relative thresholds — e.g., +30% P95 or error rate over 1% sustained for 5 minutes — but we recommend tuning per-route. for example, triage route has tighter SLAs so lower thresholds.
[04:06] Priya: would it be possible to have a two-tier gate? like first fallback to same family quantized variant, if still bad route to smaller model.
[04:14] Marcus: yep that's the tiered fallback we discussed in the doc — primary -> quantized variant -> smaller compact model -> external fallback (eg hosted tiny model). you can configure delays and cooldown windows for each step.
[04:26] Tom: cool. and about cost — what's the unit cost delta between pinned quantized variant and the compact fallback?
[04:32] Sofia: ballpark numbers on your traffic: primary quantized model is about $X per 1k tokens, fallback compact about 40% less, but again precision differs. we'll break that out in the spreadsheet.
[04:46] Priya: timeline wise, we are targeting a production freeze by May 3rd for the high-risk flows. can you support that?
[04:54] Marcus: yes we can. we recommend scheduling the freeze on a low-traffic window and we suggest running two warmed benchmark runs beforehand.
[05:02] Darren: what about rollback audit trails — we need a clear log for compliance if we cutover to fallback.
[05:08] Marcus: every routing decision is traced: model id, commit hash, latency sample, decision criteria, and which rule fired. those traces can be exported to your SIEM.
[05:18] Lisa: great. is there an escape hatch if the whole region faces an outage?
[05:21] Sofia: yes multi-region fallback is supported, though cold-starts will affect early tokens. you can also set an SLA policy to re-route to a different region's standby capacity.
[05:32] [small crosstalk] Priya: ok i want to call out one pain point — our legal team needs to sign off on data residency first. we cannot send logs out of the EU for certain routes.
[05:42] Marcus: understood — for that we recommend Private deployment in your EU region with logs persisted inside your account. we'll provide the exact KMS/HSM controls in the security pack.
[05:53] Tom: on the model naming again, could we freeze on an exact artifact hash rather than the friendly label?
[05:59] Marcus: absolutely. best practice is to pin to a model artifact id (commit hash) plus quantization profile. that gives deterministic rollbacks. friendly labels are for humans.
[06:11] Sofia: ok let's talk operational runbook — we propose the following: 1) define fence list, 2) run warmed benchmarks and acceptance evals, 3) set soft gate thresholds per route, 4) shadow for 24 hrs, 5) switch to pinned variant, 6) monitor 72 hrs with daily check-ins.
[06:30] Priya: that sequence looks good. can we compress the shadowing for low risk routes to 6 hrs?
[06:36] Marcus: yes low risk routes can have shorter shadow windows. we want at least one business cycle though to capture diurnal patterns.
[06:44] Tom: small detail — when you say warmed run, do you warm KV cache with real prefixes or synthetic ones?
[06:50] Marcus: better to use synthetic with similar distribution but real prefixes are most representative. for privacy you can hash/pseudonymize prefixes before sending.
[07:01] Priya: ok i'll coordinate with Tom on that.
[07:05] [pause]
[07:12] Darren: another question — if we detect a quality regression after a pinned release, can we automatically revert to the last known-good artifact?
[07:19] Marcus: yes — we keep a history of pinned artifacts; automatic rollback to last-known-good is an option. note that the system can either do a soft fallback (route to compact) or a hard rollback (switch artifact) depending on config. both are traceable.
[07:35] Lisa: product needs clarity on what 'last-known-good' means — is it the last artifact that passed acceptance evals or last artifact that we had in production?
[07:44] Elliot: typically it's the last artifact that passed acceptance and also had production traffic without regressions. we can expose that info in the console.
[07:54] Priya: ok thanks. next — safety nets: do you run safety checks at inference time or prefilter on prompts?
[08:01] Marcus: both. inline safety filters can be applied at runtime and you can also preprocess/prompts. for some regulated content we recommend both layers.
[08:10] Sofia: i wanted to circle back to the user-visible aspect — we can set a minimal user-facing latency increase threshold so that fallback doesn't trigger merely on small spikes that users won't notice.
[08:22] Tom: sensible. also, would we be able to run an offline eval comparing the pinned artifact to the fallback to measure drift?
[08:29] Marcus: yes we can batch sample past traffic and run offline evals; that'll give you automatic quality deltas so you can set guardrails.
[08:36] Priya: cool. what's needed from our side this week?
[08:40] Sofia: three things: final list of routes to fence, confirm the freeze date (May 3rd suggested), and permission for Redwood to run the warmed benchmark against your staging endpoints.
[08:51] Priya: we'll confirm route list by Friday.
[08:54] Darren: and about the warmed benchmark results — can you include the raw traces and the per-token latency histogram?
[08:59] Marcus: yes i'll provide raw traces and histograms.
[09:03] [short silence]
[09:08] Tom: one more technical — when switching models is there state transfer for ongoing sessions? e.g., do you preserve KV cache across variants?
[09:16] Marcus: no cross-variant KV transfer generally; you can persist session context and replay prefixes to warm cache on the new variant but direct KV reuse isn't safe across different model architectures. that means a quick cold penalty on the first few tokens after an artifact switch.
[09:34] Lisa: that matters for interactive flows. can we set a pre-warm window where traffic is duplicated to the new variant for a short time?
[09:41] Marcus: that's what warm shadowing does — duplicate a small percentage of traffic to pre-warm. we recommend at least 5% ramp for thirty minutes before full cutover for interactive flows.
[09:55] Priya: ok that's helpful.
[09:58] Sofia: logistics — i'll send the mapping doc, the trimmed results sheet, and a short runbook with recommended thresholds. Marcus will run the extra benchmark and attach traces.
[10:09] Priya: legal will review residency constraints; we'll confirm flows that must remain in EU.
[10:15] Darren: one last ask — could you include a quick section in the runbook about how to undo a pinned freeze if we need to (ie emergency escape hatch)?
[10:24] Sofia: yes we'll include an emergency unfreeze procedure with required approvals.
[10:30] [brief chatter about calendar invites]
[10:36] Sofia: ok let's summarize next steps and owners.
[10:39] Elliot: action items: Sofia send mapping + trimmed spreadsheet; Marcus run warmed runs and share raw logs; Priya confirm routes & freeze date; Redwood to provide security export doc and runbook with emergency unfreeze.
[10:55] Priya: all good. thanks everyone.
[11:00] Sofia: great, we'll follow up by Friday with artifacts and a 30-min follow-up if needed.
[11:06] meeting end
